title: Lena and the Hymn
premise: Oscar Crane returns to the village of Hallowmere to bury his twin sister Lena, only to discover the body in the coffin is not hers — and no one else seems to notice. When a church bell that was melted down in 1911 begins to ring at dusk, Oscar learns the village made a bargain generations ago: every year, one name is 'returned' to something living beneath the chapel, and in 1974 his family cheated it by substituting Lena's grandmother. The bell is calling in the debt, and it wants what was taken. To save Lena, who is still alive but slowly being erased from every memory, photograph, and record, Oscar must uncover what his grandfather stole, descend into the flooded crypt where the bell was cast, and give back the true payment — himself — before the last ring of the final night.
about_author: Ansel Ishikawa is the pen name of a former church archivist from coastal Maine who spent a decade cataloguing parish records from defunct congregations. Their fiction draws on the strange gaps and duplicated names found in those ledgers.

chapters.title: The Wrong Body
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Arriving in Hallowmere for Lena's funeral, Oscar lifts the coffin lid for a private goodbye and finds a stranger's face — older, water-bloated, wearing his mother's locket. The undertaker insists it is Lena. Emotional beat: cold disbelief masked by grief.

chapters.title: Lights On, Doors Counted
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. He refuses to leave until he finds his sister, staying at the empty family house, counting doors each night as their childhood ritual demanded. He finds Lena's diary hidden behind a panel, its last entry reading: 'It rang again. Don't answer it.' Beat: dread taking root.

chapters.title: The Bell That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Vicar Edith Marsh's POV. At dusk the church bell rings though the tower has been empty since 1911; Edith alone records it in the parish log, as her predecessors did, in a ledger of dates going back two centuries. Beat: weary complicity.

chapters.title: Everyone Knew Lena
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Villagers describe Lena warmly — but each description contradicts the last, and an old photo shows her face smearing like wet ink. Only the town drunk, Silas Fen, tells him: 'She's not dead yet. That's the problem.' Beat: isolation deepening.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Returns
chapters.summary: Edith's POV. She shows Oscar the ledger: every year since 1832 a name is written and struck through, 'returned.' In 1974 the entry reads 'Crane' — struck through twice, then overwritten with another name. Beat: horror of inherited debt.

chapters.title: What Grandfather Took
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. In the attic he finds his grandfather's letters describing the 1974 substitution: the thing below wanted a Crane twin, and the family gave the other grandmother's newborn instead. The letters end mid-sentence. Beat: betrayal across generations.

chapters.title: Silas at the Waterline
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Drunk and terrified, Silas recounts the night in 1974 when he helped carry a bundle down into the flooded crypt under the chapel. He has heard the bell every year since, growing louder. Beat: guilt as physical illness.

chapters.title: Lena Answers
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A phone call from a number that shouldn't exist: Lena's voice, calm, telling him she's fine, come find her, follow the sound. He realizes the voice knows things only Lena would know — and things she couldn't. Beat: hope curdling into manipulation.

chapters.title: The Erasure Begins
chapters.summary: Edith's POV. Records of Lena vanish: the funeral register blanks itself, mourners forget attending. Edith fights to preserve one page by copying it by hand, learning why her predecessors kept the ledger. Beat: memory as resistance.

chapters.title: Nineteen Eleven
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. In the county archive he learns the original bell was melted down after it 'would not stop ringing' following the drowning of the foundry twins, the Ashcombe girls. The metal was recast into the chapel's foundation stones. Beat: the past is structural.

chapters.title: Counted Doors, Open Mouths
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The house turns against him: doors he counted appear where walls were, and behind one he hears Lena humming their childhood hymn. He nearly opens it; the diary's warning stops him. Beat: longing weaponized.

chapters.title: The Congregation Below
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas takes Oscar to the sealed crypt entrance beneath the chapel, showing him carvings of villagers kneeling toward a submerged shape. Fresh footprints lead in — none lead out. Beat: point of no return approaching.

chapters.title: Edith's Confession
chapters.summary: Edith's POV. She admits the vicars have always chosen who gets 'returned,' and this year the ledger wrote itself: 'CRANE TWIN.' She offers Oscar a way out — write someone else's name. Beat: moral temptation.

chapters.title: A Name in Wet Ink
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Holding the ledger pen over Silas's name, Oscar sees the ink move, forming letters on its own: L-E-N-A. The book isn't a record; it's an appetite. He closes it. Beat: refusal at great cost.

chapters.title: The Hymn
chapters.summary: Lena's POV (fragmentary, dreamlike). Trapped in the flooded dark, Lena remembers only fragments — Oscar, a lullaby, cold water — and sings the hymn to keep her name intact. Each verse she forgets a word. Beat: identity dissolving.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. With Silas's rope and Edith's stolen key, Oscar enters the crypt as the bell rings continuously now. The water is warm. Something vast shifts below, patient, listening. Beat: terror and resolve entwined.

chapters.title: The Foundry Twins
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. In an air pocket he finds the Ashcombe twins — not dead, not alive, kept as the bell's first 'returns,' faces like unfinished wax. They show him the truth: the thing doesn't want a life. It wants a memory strong enough to hold a name. Beat: revelation reframing everything.

chapters.title: What Was Taken in 1974
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The stolen infant grew into the stranger in Lena's coffin — a person made of substituted names, never claimed, never remembered. Oscar realizes the debt can be paid by giving the unclaimed one back her true story. Beat: grief turning to purpose.

chapters.title: The Last Ring
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. On the final night, Oscar speaks the infant's real name aloud in the crypt while Edith reads it from the ledger above and Lena sings the completed hymn. The bell cracks mid-tone. Beat: climax, sacrifice offered and transformed.

chapters.title: Returned
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The water recedes. The stranger in the coffin becomes the woman she should have been, buried under her own name at last. Lena wakes in the guest room, remembering everything except the hymn — which Oscar hums to her, so one of them keeps it. Beat: bittersweet restoration.

chapters.title: Doors, Counted
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Weeks later, the siblings prepare to leave Hallowmere. Lena counts the doors out loud, an old ritual restored. In the chapel, Edith writes the final ledger entry: PAID IN FULL — then burns the book. Beat: release, guarded peace.

chapters.title: Coda: Bronze in the Walls
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, years later. A letter arrives from Hallowmere: the chapel is being demolished, and workers found the old bell's clapper fused into the foundation — warm to the touch, faintly ringing. Oscar drives north through the night. Final beat: debts of memory are never entirely closed.
